hypothesis: H61-G: a buried normal fault is a step in the GP-1012-calibrated inverted basement surface; the gravity step fixes a +/-1 km corridor and the in-corridor slope ridge of the detrended elevation fixes the trace to the 300 m kernel.
mechanism: Basement throw under alluvium -> isostatic-residual gradient maximum (Parker/Oldenburg inversion, Blakely-Simpson maxima, measured throw >= 80 m) -> growth of the same fault through the fill -> subtle young scarp = slope-ridge of band 19 inside the corridor.
named_non_fault_mimic: Intrabasement lithologic density contacts can produce the same gravity step without a fault; fan toes, terrace risers and channels can produce slope ridges without a fault. The conjunction is a proposed discriminator, not a demonstrated exclusion: independent density-contrast/lithology data were not used, so this competing explanation remains unresolved.
